AdminActionContext.description:
The objects the action was pressed on, as the admin passed them (checked against
the action's target).

input.description:
The form's values when the action has an `input_schema` (an object), as the
admin sent them: check them against the schema.

scope.description:
The app's scopes as far as the caller holds them, space-separated: what the
caller may have the app do for them.

oneOf.description: The staff member who pressed it (`user_…`); absent for an API key.

AdminActionResponse.description:
What the app answers: what the admin shows next. Every field is optional; `{}` is
a plain success.

message.description: Plain text to show (a toast), 1 to 500 characters.

navigate.description: A path within the app's page to go to (`/orders/ord_…`).

refresh.description: Whether the admin should reload what the action was pressed on.

Currency.description: An ISO 4217 currency code. Funds, precious metals and test codes (XDR, XAU, XXX) aren't accepted.

Email.description: An email address; stored trimmed and lowercased, so responses show it that way.

Money.description: An amount of money in one currency.

amount.description: In minor units (1050 is 10.50). At most 2^53 - 1 either way, so every amount is exact in JSON.

currency.description: An ISO 4217 currency code. Funds, precious metals and test codes (XDR, XAU, XXX) aren't accepted.

NextAction.description: What a storefront does after starting a payment.

oneOf.description: Send the buyer to the provider's page.

Mount the app's storefront element (a custom element) with these properties (a
Stripe client secret, …), and wait for its `hypha:payment-confirmed` event.

props.description: Any JSON object: the element's own properties.

oneOf.description: Show these words (a bank transfer's details); the money comes later.

PaymentActionRequest.description: What Hypha sends to capture, void or refund a payment.

oneOf.description:
How much: for a capture or refund, at most what's left; absent for the whole
(a void never has one).

attempt.description:
The attempt the payment collects through, when the app's reports named one
(`attempt` on `POST /admin/payments/{id}/events`): what to act on, where a
capture's own ID may have replaced `reference`.

oneOf.description:
The cart it was started for, and its order once placed: absent when Hypha gives back
the money of a cart whose order it couldn't place.

reference.description: The provider's ID for the payment, as the app gave it on start.

PaymentActionResponse.description:
Whether the provider took the action. Accepted isn't done: the payment moves when
the app reports the result (`POST /admin/payments/{id}/events`).

reference.description: The provider's ID for this capture or refund, when it has one.

oneOf.description: The provider said no; `reason` is shown to staff.

PaymentStartRequest.description:
What Hypha sends to start a payment. Settings for the method stay with the app (it keeps
its own): the method's ID is enough to find them.

amount.description: What to collect: the cart's total, in its currency.

cart.description:
The cart being paid for (`cart_…`). Hypha places its order once the app reports
the payment `authorized`, `processing` or `paid` (or says so when asked:
`payments.status`).

channel.description:
Where the cart is (its sales channel), to whom it sells (its market) and where it
ships (its country).

oneOf.description:
The buyer's email (for the provider's receipt). Personal data: absent unless the
app's grant has `customer_data:email`.

method.description: The payment method the buyer chose (`pm_…`), whose provider is this app.

oneOf.description:
Absent: the order doesn't exist yet. Only a payment started with its order has
one (none of an app's, today).

payment.description:
The payment Hypha created for this attempt (`pay_…`), also the call's
`Idempotency-Key`: a retried start must not charge twice.

return_url.description: Where the storefront wants the buyer back after a redirect, when it said.

PaymentStartResponse.description: The app's answer to a start: what the buyer does next.

reference.description: The provider's ID for the payment (a PaymentIntent's `pi_…`), kept on it.

PaymentState.description:
Where the shopper's money is at the provider.

Known values: `open`, `processing`, `authorized`, `paid`, `failed`, `canceled`. More may be added: treat an unknown one as you would an unexpected state, not as an error.

PaymentStatusRequest.description: What Hypha sends to ask where a payment is.

attempt.description: The attempt the payment collects through, when the app's reports named one.

oneOf.description: The cart it was started for.

reference.description: The provider's ID for the payment, as the app gave it on start.

PaymentStatusResponse.description: The app's answer: the state, and its IDs for the payment.

attempt.description: The attempt this state is about (as `attempt` on the events route).

PostalAddressResponse.description:
A postal address as Hypha sends it to an app. Personal fields (names, phone, street,
postal code, city, province) are left out without the app's `customer_data:name` /
`:phone` / `:address` scopes and listed in `redacted`: the ones every address has
(`last_name`, `line1`, `city`) are then absent, the optional ones `null`. Country and
company always come.

redacted.description: The personal fields left out for this app.

amount.description: Not negative, in the request's currency.

reference.description: The app's quote reference, copied to the order's shipping line.

service.description: The service code a shipping option names (`express`).

RateCallbackRequest.description: What Hypha sends: `POST <callback_url>` with this body.

id.description:
`rreq_…`, also sent as `Hypha-Request-Id` and `Idempotency-Key`: for the app's
logs and de-duplication.

RateEstimate.description: Business days from shipping to delivery.

weight_grams.description: One unit's weight, when the variant has one.

currency.description: The cart's currency: every rate must be in it.

oneOf.description: The address of the location that would ship the group, when it has one.

RatesResponse.description: What the app answers with a 2xx.

rates.description: The services it can ship the group with; empty when none.

SearchFacetCounts.description: A facet's values with how many hits have each, most first.

SearchGroup.description:
What one hit stands for.

Known values: `listing`, `product`, `variant`. More may be added: treat an unknown one as you would an unexpected state, not as an error.

SearchHit.description:
One hit: a product, and the variant that stands for it when the group is a variant
or a listing split by options.

SearchPriceRange.description: Inclusive bounds on a price, in minor units.

SearchQueryRequest.description: What the shopper searched for, in one market and channel.

available.description: Only what's in stock (`true`), out of stock (`false`), or either (absent).

oneOf.description: Only products in this category or one below it.

The storefront's sales channel: only products published to it. Absent for a
staff search, which sees every channel.

currency.description: The market's currency, which `price` bounds are in.

facets.description:
The facets to count (`vendor`, `product_type`, `tag`, `option.<name>`), in the
order to answer them.

filters.description:
Products with any of each filter's values; filters on different facets must all
match.

market.description: The shopper's market: what's sold to them, at its prices.

offset.description: Hits to skip, then at most `limit` (1 to 100) to answer.

price.description: Inclusive price bounds, in the currency's minor units.

query.description:
The words as the shopper typed them; empty lists everything that matches the
filters.

SearchQueryResponse.description: The app's answer: one page of hits, in order.

facets.description: One per asked-for facet, in the asked order; a facet left out counts nothing.

SearchSort.description:
The order of the hits.

Known values: `relevance`, `newest`, `price_asc`, `price_desc`, `title`. More may be added: treat an unknown one as you would an unexpected state, not as an error.

info.description: The synchronous calls Hypha makes to apps mid-flow: each is a versioned contract an app implements by registering a URL for it. A reshaped request or response is a new version.
info.title: Hypha Extension Points

post.description: `POST` to the URL the app registered for `admin.action` v1. Answer within 10000 ms (unless the app's registration sets another timeout), in at most 256 KiB, with a 2xx and the response below. Anything else (no answer, another status, a body that isn't the response) is a failure: the flow stops with `app_unavailable` (502, `details: {app, point}`). Every call is in the app's call log (`GET /admin/apps/{key}/extension-calls`).

parameters.description: `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" under the app's secret>`. Check it, and refuse a `t` more than a few minutes old.
parameters.name: Hypha-Signature

parameters.description: The point's name, as this operation's.
parameters.name: Hypha-Extension

parameters.description: The point's version.
parameters.name: Hypha-Extension-Version

parameters.description: The same for every retry of one piece of work: answer a repeat as the first.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: The store the call is for (`store_…`).
parameters.name: Hypha-Store

default.description: A failure. Apps built on `@hyphacommerce/app` answer `{code, error}` (`invalid_signature`, `unknown_extension`, `unsupported_version`, `invalid_request`, `handler_failed`); the code is kept in the call log.
